newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB says no plan to revise earnings forecast now.
newsitem.headline: NCB says no plan to revise earnings forecast now.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd said on Thursday that it has no plan at the moment to revise its earnings forecasts for the financial year which ends on March 31.

Tadao Iwaki, senior managing director of NCB, told a news conference that the bank wants to make a swift decision on its restructuring plan, but that the plan is still fluid as the bank's earning results for 1996/97 remain unclear.

Iwaki also said the long-term credit bank thinks it will be able to achieve an eight-percent capital adequacy ratio at the end of March, which is a requirement of globally operating banks set under the Bank for International Settlements (BIS).
The level of Tokyo stock prices at the end of this financial year on March 31 would be the only factor which will influence NCB's earnings results for the year, Iwaki said.
If Tokyo stock prices remain at current levels, NCB would be able to post a net profit of 15 billion yen for the current financial year as projected, Iwaki said.
Iwaki added that the bank's operating profits would likely be higher than the bank had expected and that the extra gain will be used to finance the bank's planned bad loan write-offs.

A fall in overall Tokyo stocks is widely expected to be a setback to Japanese banks already facing the difficult task of tackling mountains of bad loans, as they hope to use unrealised profit in their stock holdings to help write off problem loans, analysts say.
Earlier, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported that NCB may withdraw from its overseas operations under the restructuring plan.

An expected net loss for the second consecutive year and liquidation of its bad loans will make it almost impossible for the ailing long-term credit bank to meet the BIS capital adequacy requirements, the paper reported without citing a source.
